parsed_mutations.rationale: Aspartic acid at position 25 is part of the catalytic dyad. Substituting it with asparagine may help study the role of hydrogen bonding in catalysis without introducing a charged residue.
Isoleucine 30 is near the substrate-binding pocket. Substituting it with valine may slightly alter hydrophobic packing and provide insights into substrate specificity.
Proline 50 is located in a loop region near the active site. Replacing it with alanine could increase flexibility and help study the role of loop dynamics in enzyme function.
Valine 82 is a key residue in the substrate-binding pocket. Substituting it with threonine introduces a polar hydroxyl group, which may affect substrate interactions.
Isoleucine 84 is involved in substrate binding. Replacing it with methionine, a slightly larger hydrophobic residue, could modulate pocket size and flexibility.
Leucine 90 is near the dimer interface. Substituting it with phenylalanine may enhance π-stacking interactions and stabilize the dimer.
Asparagine 93 is located near the flap region. Substituting it with glutamine, which has a longer side chain, could affect flap dynamics and substrate accessibility.
Glycine 98 is in a flexible region near the active site. Replacing it with alanine may slightly restrict flexibility, providing insights into the role of this region in catalysis.
